title: Night Patrol of the Stone Hall
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Old Shi（Night patrol Old Shi in his fifties, gray crew cut, deep-gray security uniform and black leather shoes, patrol baton and key ring at the waist, eyes alert yet tired） pushes the door into the stone hall gallery（The main gallery floored in cold stone, celadon in the central glass case, spotlights set in the walls, clear echo）; the celadon lotus jar（A half-man-tall celadon lotus jar, plum-green glaze intact, lotus petals in relief on the belly, cold light flowing inside the glass case） stands intact on display in the glass-case cold light.

A row of five cold-white spotlights（A row of five cold-white spotlights set in the east-wall light trough of the stone hall gallery, shades wiped clear） is set in the east-wall light trough of the stone hall gallery; Old Shi checks each brightness in turn.

Two closing bronze bells（Two closing bronze bells hung at the stone-hall doorway, bodies engraved with Quiet, chiming lightly when the wind rises） hang at the stone hall doorway; Old Shi reaches out and lets them chime lightly.
Old Shi circles the glass case of the celadon lotus jar, checking seals and humidity readings.
Old Shi looks out the window toward the sky beyond the front granite plaza.
The intact celadon lotus jar stands quietly at the center of the stone hall gallery.
Old Shi sits on a stone bench and dozes in the spotlight glow.
The air conditioner hums low; Old Shi buttons the uniform collar tight.
Old Shi opens the patrol log（A deep-blue leather patrol log with the museum crest on the cover, hourly checkpoints recorded in fountain pen） and notes this hour's checkpoints in fountain pen.
Old Shi draws a humidity curve in the patrol log.
Old Shi closes the patrol log and returns it to the duty-desk drawer.
Cold light from the celadon lotus jar sweeps Old Shi's profile.
Old Shi gently wipes fingerprints from the glass case with a soft cloth.

On the front granite plaza（The granite-step plaza before the museum, flagpoles and guide boards in rows, night lamps turning the stone cyan） at dawn, Old Shi greets young Maisui（Young Maisui: a lean museum intern of sixteen, wheat-yellow scarf, light-gray vest, a celadon-shard badge on the left lapel, bright stubborn eyes） driving up in deep-blue Nightwatch（A deep-blue patrol electric cart with white Nightwatch lettering on the door, basket holding a flood flashlight and seal rolls）.
Maisui jumps down from Nightwatch and retightens the wheat-yellow scarf.
Old Shi points to the three thermo-hygrometers（Three white thermo-hygrometers set by case number on the stone stand beside the celadon case） on the stone stand and teaches Maisui the safe ranges.
Maisui crouches on the granite steps and curiously traces the relief letters on the guide board.
Old Shi points to the stone-hall lintel and explains the closing route to Maisui.
Maisui looks back at parked Nightwatch, eyes full of longing.
They lean side by side on a flagpole, listening to distant morning city noise.

In the storage dark corridor（A narrow dark corridor to the artifact storage, safes and hygrometers on both sides, only emergency lights dim yellow）, Aye（Young Aye: face closely matching Maisui's, but ochre scarf, a film-roll badge on the right lapel, more swaggering look） in an ochre scarf glances back from behind a safe.
Aye fiddles with a hygrometer in the dark corridor; the film-roll badge glints lightly.
Aye snaps the storage-zone numbers on the wall with a phone, smiling with swagger.
Aye carries a camera through the shadow of the storage dark corridor.
Emergency lights flicker; Aye stops to hear the overhead duct hum.
On the front granite plaza, Maisui and Aye stand side by side—one wheat-yellow scarf, one ochre scarf.
Maisui hands Aye a thermo-hygrometer; they smile at each other.
Aye smooths Maisui's scarf; they walk slowly down the stone steps.
Maisui and Aye part at the east end of the plaza, each walking opposite ways.
Night lamps come on; their backs—one yellow, one ochre—slowly pull apart.
Months later at night, Old Shi keeps watch alone in the stone hall gallery; the celadon lotus jar stands quiet on display.

Old Shi opens the patrol log（The same patrol log stained by a spilled ink bottle, cover blackened, writing bled into ink blotches） and finds the cover stained by an ink bottle, writing bled into ink blotches.
Old Shi wipes mist from the glass case of the celadon lotus jar.
Old Shi looks out toward the black front granite plaza.
The outline of the celadon lotus jar slowly resolves under the spotlights.
Old Shi slips the stained patrol log into a file pouch and sighs.
Seasons turn; Old Shi pushes the door into the stone hall gallery day after day.
Another snowy night, Old Shi wraps his uniform tight beside the celadon lotus jar.
At spring install, Old Shi checks seal numbers in the stone hall.
At high summer noon, Old Shi wipes glass-case rims dried by the air conditioner.
Through autumn rain, cold light on the celadon lotus jar turns dull in the damp.
Another New Year's Eve, Old Shi keeps the stone hall gallery alone until dawn.
The night before a special show, Old Shi calibrates the thermo-hygrometers two hours early.
On a full-moon night, Old Shi sets all spotlights to display level.
When a cold snap hits, Old Shi hangs a wind curtain on the stone-hall door.
Around Qingming, Old Shi sweeps leaves and grit from the front granite plaza.
In plum-rain season, Old Shi checks storage humidity again and again for overruns.
On the first frost of winter, Old Shi's white breath drifts under the spotlights.
In anti-theft drill week, Old Shi tests every checkpoint sensor once.
On New Year's duty, Old Shi sorts the key ring beside the duty desk.
On a blizzard night with roads closed, Old Shi paces the stone hall listening to the wind.
For three visitor-free nights running, Old Shi memorizes the checkpoint order again and again.
One night humidity spikes; Old Shi has to add a dehumidifier.
The glass case clicks lightly; Old Shi looks up at once to check the celadon lotus jar.
At three a.m. Old Shi sips ice-cold tea from a thermos.
He sorts the thermo-hygrometer numbers by the stone stand.
The closing bronze bells chime lightly in the wind; Old Shi looks up to listen.
As the sky pales, Old Shi logs the last checkpoint set of the night.
Before locking the hall, he takes one last look at the intact glaze of the celadon lotus jar.
After the rain stops, he sweeps pooled water on the steps toward the drain.
At daybreak Old Shi patrols the front granite plaza; deep-blue Nightwatch is parked by the flagpole.
Old Shi crouches to check Nightwatch tires and the seal rolls in the basket.
Old Shi walks to the stone stand; those three thermo-hygrometers still sit in neat order.

A strange gray-white works truck（A strange gray-white works pickup with barrier boards in the bed, no Nightwatch lettering—nothing like Nightwatch） drives along the park road, barrier boards in the bed—not Nightwatch.
Old Shi stands on the granite steps and records last night's humidity peak.
Old Shi straightens the guide board again.
Distant morning fog lifts, revealing deeper city outlines.
Nearby construction tremor rises suddenly; the stone hall gallery shudders uneasily; the celadon lotus jar rocks hard.
The glass case hums; Old Shi rushes to the emergency brace frame.

A crisp crack—spiderweb cracks burst across the celadon lotus jar（The same celadon lotus jar with spiderweb cracks across the glaze, rim slightly chipped, cold light splintering at the cracks） glaze; the rim chips slightly.
On the park road, deep-blue Nightwatch jolts hard in a sharp turn.
One impact sends Nightwatch（The deep-blue electric cart hits the steps, nose dented, basket spilled—wreckage that can no longer patrol） into the steps, nose dented, basket spilled.
In the stone hall, Old Shi lunges at the glass case and fiercely steadies the rocking celadon lotus jar.
The day after the tremor, Old Shi stands in the stone hall gallery staring at the cracked celadon lotus jar.
Old Shi traces the crack path through the glass with a finger, face dark.
On a sticky note beside the patrol log, Old Shi writes the date Nightwatch was wrecked.
An old photo of Nightwatch hangs on the stone-hall wall; Old Shi gazes long.
Old Shi takes down one of the five cold-white spotlights from the east wall and sits alone in the faint light.
The damaged celadon lotus jar still stands cracked at the center of the glass case.
Weeks later Old Shi helps the restorer bring glue tools and begins repairing the celadon lotus jar.

Old Shi takes a fake lotus jar（A half-man-tall fake lotus jar shaped like the celadon lotus jar but grayer glaze and shallower relief） from a wooden crate—it looks like the celadon lotus jar but with grayer glaze.
The restorer carefully glues and fills; Old Shi steadies the base beside.

The last repair line is polished smooth; the celadon lotus jar（The celadon lotus jar returns to display after glue repair and fill; fine repair lines remain on the glaze, distinct from the original intact state） enters its glued-repaired state.
The repaired celadon lotus jar returns to display; Old Shi looks at it with relief.

A light-green Cleaner One（A brand-new light-green cleaning electric cart with Cleaner One on the door, mop buckets in the bed—nothing like Nightwatch） rolls onto the front granite plaza—nothing like the already-wrecked Nightwatch.

Security director Old Chu（Security director Old Chu in his fifties, gray crew cut and deep-gray uniform close to Old Shi's build, but gold director insignia on the shoulder boards） walks onto the plaza and talks shoulder to shoulder with Old Shi; their builds are alike.
Old Chu points at Cleaner One and explains the new park roster to Old Shi.
Cleaner One drives off; Old Shi alone watches it leave the plaza.
Wind flaps the roster sheet Old Chu left behind.

Outside the museum arrives volunteer docent Xiaosu（Volunteer docent Xiaosu, sixteen or seventeen, wheat-yellow scarf; at a glance like young Maisui, but no celadon-shard badge on the left lapel, shy unfamiliar eyes） in a wheat-yellow scarf; at a glance she looks somewhat like young Maisui.
Xiaosu tries reading the guide board, but Old Shi shakes his head—she is not Maisui after all.
Xiaosu leaves the front granite plaza with tour leaflets; her back fades down the park road.

Years later at dusk, Old Shi（The same Old Shi after a knee injury: right-knee brace, walking slowly on an aluminum crutch, still in that faded deep-gray uniform） with a right-knee brace leans on an aluminum crutch outside the stone hall gallery.
Old Shi looks up at the lintel on his crutch, gaze far away.
Those two closing bronze bells at the doorway chime lightly in the wind; Old Shi stops on his crutch to listen.
On his crutch Old Shi presses a palm to the cold stone wall of the hall, as if saying goodbye.
He slowly sits on the steps, braced leg stretched straight.

By day, adult Maisui（Adult Maisui: an upright docent in her twenties, still in wheat-yellow scarf with celadon-shard badge, steady manner） returns along the park road and hurries toward the stone hall gallery.
Maisui reunites with crutch-leaning Old Shi outside the door; they embrace.
By the narrow duty-room bed, Maisui holds Old Shi's thick but ice-cold hand.
Old Shi（Old Shi lies still on the narrow duty-room bed with eyes closed, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies.
Maisui gently sets Old Shi's patrol baton back by the pillow.
Old Shi's deep-gray uniform still hangs behind the stone-hall door; Maisui reaches out and gently strokes it.

By the lintel, adult Maisui stands before a newly nailed founding brass plaque（A founding brass plaque nailed to the stone-hall lintel, carved with Old Shi's name and founding year, edges mottled with verdigris）.
Maisui's fingertip traces Old Shi's name carved on the founding brass plaque.
Wind rises; closing bronze bells chime faintly afar; Maisui lifts her head.

Adult Aye（Adult Aye: face closely matching adult Maisui's, still in ochre scarf with film-roll badge, camera on the shoulder） arrives from the imaging department and embraces Maisui tightly outside the stone hall.
Maisui and Aye stand side by side by the lintel—one calm, one swaggering.
They look at each other in silence, faces similar yet different.
Aye raises the camera, then quietly lowers it, only standing with Maisui.
The shot returns years—that youth tracing guide-board relief letters on the granite steps appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the stone hall, a plum-green glaze lotus jar is lit by spotlights for the first time.
Flash back to the storage dark corridor that year—a figure in an ochre scarf with a film-roll badge flashes past.
Again that row of five cold-white old trough lamps on the east wall.
Back to that granite-step plaza of first meeting; flagpoles in rows as before.
Maisui reopens the ink-stained patrol log and walks into the stone hall gallery.
On the stone stand, those three thermo-hygrometers still sit in neat order.
Maisui takes over watch of the celadon lotus jar; cold light flows again.
Outside the stone hall, the step outline slowly clears in morning light.
